article.name: סַלמָונ
article.summary: The Peshitta names Salmon as the father of Boaz by Rahab. The verse identifies him by this relationship and gives no derivation for his name.

analysis.evidence: In סַלמָונ אַולֵדֿ לבָֿעָז מֵנ רָחָבֿ, Salmon is the father, the prefixed ל marks Boaz as the child he fathered, and מֵנ רָחָבֿ identifies Rahab as the mother. Boaz then takes Salmon’s place as subject of the same verb in the next clause.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix. Subject of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: The personal name of the father of Boaz.

article.name: בָּעָז
article.note: The Syriac name is keyed by its consonants בעז. The link to עזז through Hebrew עֹז, “strength”, is tentative. Matthew gives no etymology.
article.summary: Matthew names Boaz as the son of Salmon and Rahab and the father of Obed by Ruth. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

analysis.evidence: סַלמָונ אַולֵדֿ לבָֿעָז מֵנ רָחָבֿ names Boaz as the child Salmon fathered by Rahab. The next clause repeats the name without ל as its subject, בָּעָז אַולֵדֿ לעֻובִֿידֿ, “Boaz fathered Obed”.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed ל marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ, “fathered”.
analysis.sense: Boaz, the son of Salmon and Rahab and the father of Obed.

analysis.evidence: Salmon fathers Boaz מֵנ רָחָבֿ, “by Rahab.” The next clause repeats the construction when Boaz fathers Obed מֵנ רָעֻותֿ, “by Ruth.” In each clause מֵנ introduces the mother’s name.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preceding preposition מֵנ is a separate word.

article.name: עֻובִֿידֿ
article.summary: Matthew names Obed as the son of Boaz and Ruth and the father of Jesse. His Syriac name corresponds to Hebrew עוֹבֵד in Ruth, the participial form of עבד, “serve, work”.

analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed ל marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ, “fathered”.
analysis.sense: Obed, son of Boaz and Ruth and father of Jesse.

article.summary: Matthew’s Syriac genealogy names רָעֻותֿ as the mother of Obed by Boaz. The book of Ruth calls her רוּת. The meaning of her name is uncertain.

analysis.morphology: Feminine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix, governed by the separate preposition מֵנ.

article.name: אִישַי
article.summary: The Peshitta names Obed’s son אִישַי. The Hebrew genealogy in Ruth calls him יִשַׁי and names David as his son. Neither genealogy explains the name’s meaning.

conflicts: resolve the bearer and validate its name article against the current lexicon

analysis.evidence: In עֻובִֿידֿ אַולֵדֿ לִאישַי, “Obed fathered Jesse,” Jesse occupies the same position after אַולֵדֿ that Obed occupies in the preceding clause. The prefixed ל marks the child being named.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed ל marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ.
